newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission says it may cut malt barley refunds.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission says it may cut malt barley refunds.

text.p: The European Commission is concerned about the level of applications for malting barley export licences, it told the European Union's cereals management committee on Thursday.
"There was a discussion about where the demand was coming from and the Commission is edgy about it," an EU official said on Friday.
The Commission indicated that it was considering the level of refunds but was monitoring the situation, the official added.
Exports, at over 1.9 million tonnes, are above the expected 1.8 to 1.9 million forecast by the Commission.
No cut in the refund was made because the Commission said that maltsters were working at full capacity to meet existing contracts.

The committee heard that some exports were carried forward from last year because of the negative corrective applied by the Commission and because of Eastern European licences which were taken out in July.

"These two factors have inflated this year's export figures but the Commission has made it clear that it is closely monitoring the situation in the light of its GATT export limit responsibilities," the official said.
